title: Salvation and Grace - Episode 7: Good Shepherd Opens the Door to Divine Knowing

parts.style: warm, gentle late-night welcome, a soft smile in the voice, speaking slowly
parts.text: Welcome to Salvation and Grace. I'm Sarah Mitchell. <short pause> As the day winds down, we're resting in one quiet, steady truth... <short pause> the Good Shepherd knows you by name.

parts.style: tender, intimate, very soft, speaking slowly
parts.text: Tonight may be our last evening together in this series. <short pause> But this isn't goodbye... <chuckle> I'm sure we'll meet again.

In the tenth chapter of John's Gospel, Jesus speaks in pictures his first listeners would have understood immediately. <short pause> He talks about sheep and shepherds, about doors and pastures, about safety and danger. <short pause> But woven through these familiar images is something that goes deeper than any comparison. <short pause> Jesus is telling us who he is, and he is telling us that he knows who we are.
The passage begins with Jesus calling himself the door of the sheep.
Then said Jesus unto them again, Verily, verily, I say unto you, I am the door of the sheep. <long pause>

A door is the one point of access, the single way in and the single way out. <short pause> In the world Jesus knew, a shepherd would sometimes sleep across the opening of the fold at night, his own body serving as the gate. <short pause> Nothing could come in or go out without passing by him. <short pause> Jesus places himself in that position for his own.

He says that all who came before him were thieves and robbers. <short pause> He is speaking of false messiahs, of teachers who promise rescue but deliver only harm. <short pause> The true sheep did not listen to them because something in those voices did not ring true.
Then Jesus makes a promise.
I am the door: by me if any man enter in, he shall be saved, and shall go in and out, and find pasture. <long pause>

To enter by him means to come to God through him, not through your own merit or effort or spiritual achievement. <short pause> And the promise is safety and freedom together. <short pause> You shall be saved, and you shall go in and out and find pasture.
The thief comes only to steal and kill and destroy. <short pause> But Jesus says he came that his sheep might have life, and have it more abundantly.
This abundance is not wealth or comfort. <short pause> It is the fullness of life that comes from being known and loved by God.
Then the image shifts slightly.
I am the good shepherd: the good shepherd giveth his life for the sheep. <long pause>

A hired hand works for wages and runs when danger comes, because the sheep are not his own. <short pause> But the good shepherd owns the flock, and the flock belongs to him, and he does not abandon them. <short pause> He lays down his life.
Jesus is not speaking theoretically. <short pause> When he spoke these words, the cross was already ahead of him, and he knew it. <short pause> He was describing what he was about to do.
And then he speaks the words that gather everything together.
I am the good shepherd, and know my sheep, and am known of mine. <short pause> As the Father knoweth me, even so know I the Father: and I lay down my life for the sheep. <long pause>

To be known by Christ is not to be observed from a distance or assessed by a set of standards. <short pause> It is to be known in the way the Father knows the Son and the Son knows the Father. <short pause> It is an intimate, unbreakable knowing, the kind of knowing that holds nothing back.

parts.style: tender, intimate, very soft, speaking slowly
parts.text: Jesus knows your name. <short pause> He knows the weight you have carried today and the thoughts that have circled in your mind as you lie here in the dark. <short pause> He knows what you regret and what you fear. <short pause> He knows the places where you have failed and the places where you have tried and found yourself too weak.
And his knowing is not the knowing of a judge looking for fault. <short pause> It is the knowing of a shepherd who has already decided to lay down his life.

parts.style: tender, intimate, very soft, speaking slowly
parts.text: You do not have to wonder tonight whether you are seen. <short pause> You do not have to work to get his attention or prove that you deserve his care. <exhales> You are already known, completely and without condition.
The door is not closed to you. <short pause> The door is a person, and that person is Christ, and he has opened the way to the Father.

parts.style: tender, intimate, very soft, speaking slowly
parts.text: As you rest now, let that truth settle around you. <short pause> You are one of his sheep, and he knows your voice, and you are safe.
Let us pray. <short pause> Lord Jesus, you know my name and you know my heart. <short pause> Teach me to rest in the safety of your love, now and always.
Thank you for spending these evenings with me. <short pause> Until we meet again... <short pause> goodnight.
